discriminatingExperiments.verdict: gap is PEI's own semantics: per-tick ImplYield(isActive(), false) does not converge to what InnerYield(false, true)-to-quiescence reaches, so the matching payload lags one placement. NOTE loop() and PEI differ in TWO parameters (bWait and bHandleAllCurrentEvents) plus PEI's outer loop; not yet isolated. Mechanism lead: with bHandleAllCurrentEvents=false ImplYield returns early after DispatchUserEvents, skipping CheckTimeout() which upstream's own comment says invokes the scheduler.

finding021Candidate1.retractedMeasurement: GetMostUrgentTaskPriority()==-1 carried no information: the probe samples only when timeoutUs != 0, which implies CheckTimeout() returned false, which is the same condition as that function's own early return. Withdrawn as evidence.
finding021Candidate1.openSoundnessGap: RETRACTED 2026-08-06 (second review). The claim was that a lagging payload clears the stale flag; it does not. The engine's formatStateStale is true in every search row of both browsers, and updateEditorFormatState clears the flag before emitting the event, so no payload can arrive without clearing it. The misread field was the harness's own fresh = formatStateEventsObserved > 0, whose count starts before placement (web/e2-format-discovery-app.js:242,268) and so includes broadcasts caused by the placement itself.
finding021Candidate1.residualGap: one formatStateStale flag guards five fields: any watched payload (e.g. .uno:Bold) clears it, after which a list precondition may read a listBullet never re-broadcast for this paragraph. Per-field generation marking is what is missing. INFERRED, no instance observed; deprioritised under product route C, mandatory if route A is ever enabled.
finding021Candidate1.productRoute: C -- the product does not read precondition state. Closed actions dispatch unconditionally and are judged by postcondition only (post-dispatch state + saved ODT, verified 5/5). documented-state-noop is dropped rather than promised. Removes the pump dependency entirely. Route A (product calls the pump itself) is deferred, not rejected. Decided 2026-08-06; the user also decided not to file upstream.
finding021Candidate1.supportedEntryPointCorrection: the earlier claim that no supported refresh entry point exists was wrong: Scheduler::ProcessEventsToIdle() is public API (include/vcl/scheduler.hxx:65, class VCL_DLLPUBLIC Scheduler final) with production callers in sw/source/uibase/dbui/dbmgr.cxx:1375, sw/source/ui/dbui/mmresultdialogs.cxx:712 and vcl/source/app/svmain.cxx:438. Only the C wrapper unit_lok_process_events_to_idle (svapp.cxx:485-491) is labelled test-only. The real constraint is the header's own busy-lock warning, which is ours to bound. Note the doc comment claiming it calls Application::Reschedule(true) is stale; the implementation uses InnerYield(false, true).

openAfterThisRevision: The format barrier has no engine-side deadline. A client timeout leaves it active and every later caret mover gets BUSY -- observed once (A5 styled-list attempt-04, before the dispatch-path fix). Unreachable on the normal path now, but the shape is 'one timeout wedges the session'.

The caret restore is a document coordinate captured before dispatch, and the dispatch changes the paragraph's geometry. BUSY narrows who can reach it; it does not close it. A paragraph-identity anchor would, and LOK exposes none.
